decisions.reason: As in English, the whole church is addressed, women and men; "frères" stays available as the traditional form. Agreeing words follow the noun and need no span ("mes chers frères et sœurs").

decisions.choice: mwili na damu
decisions.reason: "Mwili na damu" is the Swahili way of naming human beings as they are now, mortal and weak (meaning decision), as in Hebrews 2:14; Readable speaks of "miili yetu ya nyama na damu" (our bodies of flesh and blood), as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "thịt và huyết" (L, B) for sarx kai haima; "thân thể bằng xương bằng thịt ... như hiện nay" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Greek order and picture, as the Vietnamese Ephesians 6:12 does at Literal for the reverse order; Readable says what is meant, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "혈과 육" (L); "살과 피로 된 몸" (B); "지금 그대로의 살과 피로 된 우리 몸" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Ephesians 6:12 (L) for "flesh and blood"; the meaning decision reads it as human beings as they now are, mortal and weak.

source.text: ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω· πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα, ἐν ἀτόμῳ, ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ σάλπιγγι· σαλπίσει γάρ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: Look, a mystery to you I tell: all not we will sleep, all but we will be changed, \v 52 in an instant, in a blink of an eye, at the last trumpet; it will sound for, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.

en.L: Look, I am telling you a mystery: not all of us will fall asleep, but all of us will be changed, \v 52 in an instant, in [the] blink of an eye, at the last trumpet; for it will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
en.B: Listen, I am telling you a mystery. Not all of us will die, but all of us will be changed, \v 52 in an instant, in the blink of an eye, when the last trumpet sounds. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised, never again to decay, and we who are alive will be changed.
en.R: Listen, I will tell you a mystery, something God has now made known. Not all of us will die, but God will change all of us. \v 52 It will happen in an instant, as fast as you can blink an eye, when the last trumpet sounds. Yes, the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised with bodies that can never decay. And those of us who are still alive will be changed.

fr.L: Voici, je vous dis un mystère : nous ne nous endormirons pas tous, mais tous nous serons changés, \v 52 en un instant, en un clin d’œil, à la dernière trompette ; car elle sonnera, et les morts seront ressuscités incorruptibles, et nous, nous serons changés.
fr.B: Écoutez, je vais vous dire un mystère. Nous ne mourrons pas tous, mais nous serons tous changés, \v 52 en un instant, en un clin d’œil, quand sonnera la dernière trompette. Car la trompette sonnera, et les morts seront ressuscités pour ne plus jamais se décomposer, et nous qui serons encore en vie, nous serons changés.
fr.R: Écoutez, je vais vous dire un mystère, un secret que Dieu fait maintenant connaître. Nous ne mourrons pas tous, mais Dieu nous changera tous. \v 52 Cela se passera en un instant, aussi vite qu’un clin d’œil, quand la dernière trompette sonnera. Oui, la trompette sonnera, et les morts reviendront à la vie avec un corps qui ne pourra jamais se décomposer. Et ceux d’entre nous qui seront encore vivants seront changés.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo un misterio: no todos dormiremos, pero todos seremos transformados, \v 52 en un instante, en un abrir y cerrar de ojos, en la última trompeta; porque sonará, y los muertos serán resucitados incorruptibles, y nosotros seremos transformados.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo un misterio. No todos moriremos, pero todos seremos transformados, \v 52 en un instante, en un abrir y cerrar de ojos, cuando suene la última trompeta. Porque la trompeta sonará, y los muertos resucitarán para nunca más corromperse, y nosotros, los que estemos vivos, seremos transformados.
es.R: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} voy a contar un misterio, algo que Dios ahora ha dado a conocer. No todos moriremos, pero Dios nos transformará a todos. \v 52 Sucederá en un instante, en lo que dura un parpadeo, cuando suene la última trompeta. Sí, la trompeta sonará, y los muertos serán resucitados con cuerpos que nunca podrán descomponerse. Y los que todavía estemos vivos seremos transformados.

sw.L: Tazama, nawaambia siri: hatutalala sote, lakini sote tutabadilishwa, \v 52 katika kitambo kimoja, kufumba na kufumbua jicho, wakati wa tarumbeta ya mwisho; kwa maana [tarumbeta] italia, na wafu watafufuliwa wasioharibika, nasi tutabadilishwa.
sw.B: Sikilizeni, nawaambia siri. Hatutafariki sote, lakini sote tutabadilishwa, \v 52 papo hapo, kufumba na kufumbua, tarumbeta ya mwisho itakapolia. Kwa maana tarumbeta italia, na wafu watafufuliwa wasiharibike tena, nasi tulio hai tutabadilishwa.
sw.R: Sikilizeni, nitawaambia siri, jambo ambalo Mungu ametujulisha sasa. Hatutakufa sote, lakini Mungu atatubadilisha sote. \v 52 Itatokea ghafla, kufumba na kufumbua, tarumbeta ya mwisho itakapolia. Ndiyo, tarumbeta italia, na wafu watafufuliwa wakiwa na miili isiyoweza kuoza kamwe. Nasi tutakaokuwa bado hai tutabadilishwa.

vi.L: Kìa, tôi nói cho anh chị em một sự mầu nhiệm: không phải tất cả chúng ta đều sẽ ngủ, nhưng tất cả chúng ta đều sẽ được biến đổi, \v 52 trong giây lát, trong chớp mắt, khi tiếng kèn cuối cùng; vì kèn sẽ thổi, và người chết sẽ được sống lại không hề hư nát, và chúng ta sẽ được biến đổi.
vi.B: Hãy nghe đây, tôi nói cho anh chị em một sự mầu nhiệm. Không phải tất cả chúng ta đều sẽ qua đời, nhưng tất cả chúng ta đều sẽ được biến đổi, \v 52 trong giây lát, trong nháy mắt, khi tiếng kèn cuối cùng vang lên. Vì kèn sẽ thổi, và người chết sẽ được sống lại, không bao giờ hư nát nữa, và chúng ta là những người còn sống sẽ được biến đổi.
vi.R: Hãy nghe đây, tôi sẽ nói cho anh chị em một sự mầu nhiệm, là điều mà nay Đức Chúa Trời đã bày tỏ. Không phải tất cả chúng ta đều sẽ chết, nhưng Đức Chúa Trời sẽ biến đổi tất cả chúng ta. \v 52 Điều đó sẽ xảy ra trong giây lát, nhanh như một cái chớp mắt, khi tiếng kèn cuối cùng vang lên. Phải, kèn sẽ thổi, và người chết sẽ được sống lại với thân thể không bao giờ mục nát. Và những ai trong chúng ta còn sống sẽ được biến đổi.

ko.L: 보십시오, 내가 여러분에게 비밀을 말합니다. 우리가 모두 잠들 것이 아니라 모두 변화될 것입니다. \v 52 순식간에, 눈 깜짝할 사이에, 마지막 나팔 소리에 [그렇게 될 것입니다]. 나팔 소리가 울리면 죽은 사람들은 썩지 않을 [몸으로] 살아나고, 우리는 변화될 것입니다.
ko.B: 들어 보십시오. 내가 여러분에게 비밀을 하나 말하겠습니다. 우리가 모두 죽는 것이 아니라 모두 변화될 것입니다. \v 52 마지막 나팔이 울릴 때, 순식간에, 눈 깜짝할 사이에 그렇게 될 것입니다. 나팔이 울리면, 죽은 사람들은 다시는 썩지 않을 몸으로 살아나고, 살아 있는 우리는 변화될 것입니다.
ko.R: 들어 보십시오. 하나님께서 이제 알려 주신 비밀을 여러분에게 말하겠습니다. 우리 모두가 죽지는 않을 것입니다. 그러나 하나님께서 우리 모두를 변화시키실 것입니다. \v 52 그 일은 눈을 한 번 깜박이는 것보다 더 빨리, 순식간에 일어날 것입니다. 마지막 나팔이 울릴 때 일어날 것입니다. 그렇습니다. 나팔이 울리면 죽은 사람들은 결코 썩지 않을 몸으로 다시 살아날 것입니다. 그리고 아직 살아 있는 우리는 변화될 것입니다.

pt.L: Vejam, eu lhes digo um mistério: nem todos nós adormeceremos, mas todos nós seremos transformados, \v 52 num instante, num piscar de olhos, na última trombeta; pois ela soará, e os mortos serão ressuscitados incorruptíveis, e nós seremos transformados.
pt.B: Escutem, eu lhes digo um mistério. Nem todos nós vamos morrer, mas todos seremos transformados, \v 52 num instante, num piscar de olhos, quando soar a última trombeta. Pois a trombeta vai soar, e os mortos serão ressuscitados para nunca mais se decompor, e nós, os que estivermos vivos, seremos transformados.
pt.R: Escutem, vou contar a vocês um mistério, algo que Deus agora deu a conhecer. Nem todos nós vamos morrer, mas Deus vai transformar todos nós. \v 52 Isso vai acontecer num instante, tão rápido quanto um piscar de olhos, quando soar a última trombeta. Sim, a trombeta vai soar, e os mortos serão ressuscitados com corpos que nunca podem se decompor. E nós, que ainda estivermos vivos, seremos transformados.

decisions.choice: mystery: part of God's plan once hidden and now made known
decisions.reason: μυστήριον is God's purpose, hidden until he reveals it (2:7; Romans 11:25). The mystery here is what will happen to believers who are alive when Christ comes.

decisions.choice: fall asleep: die, said of believers
decisions.reason: κοιμηθησόμεθα is used of believers who have died (11:30; 15:6, 15:18, 15:20; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-15). It looks forward to waking at the resurrection.

decisions.choice: not all of us will die
alternatives: "all of us will not die", meaning none will die
decisions.reason: The negative stands next to πάντες ("all"), so it denies "all": some will die, but not everyone. All, living and dead, will be changed.

decisions.choice: in an instant, in the blink of an eye: the change will happen all at once
decisions.reason: ἀτόμῳ is what cannot be cut or divided, the smallest piece of time. ῥιπῇ is a quick movement, here of the eye: a blink or a glance.

decisions.choice: the last trumpet: the trumpet that announces God's final coming and the gathering of his people
alternatives: the last in a numbered series of trumpets
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament the trumpet announces the day of the Lord and the gathering of God's people (Isaiah 27:13; Joel 2:1; Zechariah 9:14). Jesus and Paul link it with the coming of the Son of Man and the raising of the dead (Matthew 24:31; 1 Thessalonians 4:16). "Last" means the one at the end.

decisions.choice: we: believers still alive at that moment, among whom Paul counts himself as one who may be
alternatives: Paul is certain he will be alive
decisions.reason: The "we" is set against "the dead", so it means those alive at Christ's coming, as in 1 Thessalonians 4:15-17. Paul speaks as one who may be among them; elsewhere he reckons with his own death (2 Corinthians 5:1-8; Philippians 1:20-23).

decisions.choice: will be changed: God will change them
decisions.reason: The passive ἀλλαγησόμεθα leaves God unnamed as the one who acts, as is common in Scripture; verse 57 names God as the giver of the victory.

decisions.choice: blink of an eye
decisions.reason: "Twinkling" is the traditional word, but in modern English it is used of stars. "Blink" is the movement Paul describes (m4).

decisions.choice: fall asleep (L); die (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m2), as at 11:30; Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: something God has now made known (R); God will change (R); we who are alive (B); those of us who are still alive (R)
alternatives: a mystery; we will be changed
decisions.reason: Readable explains "mystery" (m1) and names God as the one who changes (m7). Balanced and Readable say who "we" are (m6).

decisions.choice: Look (L); Listen (B, R)
decisions.reason: ἰδοὺ calls for attention; "behold" is no longer used.

decisions.choice: imperishable (L); never again to decay (B); with bodies that can never decay (R)
decisions.reason: ἄφθαρτοι is the adjective of the noun in verse 42. Balanced and Readable say it with a verb, which reads more naturally after "raised".

decisions.choice: nous ne nous endormirons pas tous (L); nous ne mourrons pas tous (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the picture of falling asleep, which French also uses of death; Balanced and Readable give its meaning (m2). "S’endormir" rather than "dormir" because the verb says the moment of dying.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} (L); {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word "look" is said to the whole church, so it is plural; Literal says "miren", as the settled terms do for speech, and Balanced and Readable "escuchen", as the English "Listen".

decisions.choice: dormiremos (L); moriremos (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6: "dormir" for the idiom at Literal, "morir" at Balanced and Readable (m2).

decisions.choice: kufumba na kufumbua (jicho)
decisions.reason: "Kufumba na kufumbua" (shutting and opening the eye) is the Swahili idiom for something done in the blink of an eye, so it serves every level; Literal adds "jicho" (eye) as the Greek names it.

decisions.choice: hatutalala sote
decisions.reason: Swahili places "sote" after the negative verb to say "not all of us", which the Greek means (meaning decision); "sote hatutalala" would say "none of us will sleep".

decisions.choice: "Kìa" (L), "Hãy nghe đây" (B, R) for idou; "ngủ" (L), "qua đời" (B), "chết" (R), as in 7:39
decisions.reason: "Kìa" is the Literal word for idou in the Vietnamese Galatians 1:20; Balanced and Readable say "listen", as the English does. "Sự mầu nhiệm" is kept at every level, with Readable adding that God has now made it known, as in 2:7.

decisions.choice: "우리가 모두 잠들 것이 아니라" (L), "우리가 모두 죽는 것이 아니라" (B), "우리 모두가 죽지는 않을 것입니다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the negative denies "all": some will die, but not everyone. Korean "모두 ... 것이 아니라" and "모두가 ... 지는 않다" say "not all", where "모두 ... 않다" would mean "none".

decisions.choice: "변화되다" for being changed; "살아나다" for being raised; "나팔" for the trumpet
decisions.reason: "변화되다" is the word of Romans 12:2 for being changed; the meaning decision reads the passive as God changing them, which Readable says.

source.text: δεῖ γὰρ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀθανασίαν.

records.literal_gloss: It is necessary for the perishable this to put on imperishability and the mortal this to put on immortality.

en.L: For it is necessary [that] this perishable [body] put on imperishability, and [that] this mortal [body] put on immortality.
en.B: This perishable body has to put on imperishability like a garment, and this mortal body has to put on immortality.
en.R: Our bodies that can decay must be clothed with a life that cannot decay. Our bodies that can die must be clothed with a life that never ends.

fr.L: Car il faut que ce [corps] corruptible revête l’incorruptibilité, et que ce [corps] mortel revête l’immortalité.
fr.B: Ce corps périssable doit être revêtu de ce qui ne périt pas, comme d’un vêtement, et ce corps mortel doit être revêtu de l’immortalité.
fr.R: Notre corps, qui peut se décomposer, doit être habillé d’une vie qui ne se décompose pas. Notre corps, qui peut mourir, doit être habillé d’une vie qui ne finit jamais.

es.L: Porque es necesario que esto corruptible se vista de incorrupción, y esto mortal se vista de inmortalidad.
es.B: Este cuerpo corruptible tiene que revestirse de incorrupción, como de un vestido, y este cuerpo mortal tiene que revestirse de inmortalidad.
es.R: Nuestros cuerpos, que pueden descomponerse, tienen que ser revestidos de una vida que no se descompone. Nuestros cuerpos, que pueden morir, tienen que ser revestidos de una vida que nunca termina.

sw.L: Kwa maana ni lazima [mwili] huu unaoharibika uvae kutoharibika, na [mwili] huu unaokufa uvae kutokufa.
sw.B: Mwili huu unaoharibika lazima uvae kutoharibika kama vazi, na mwili huu unaokufa lazima uvae kutokufa.
sw.R: Miili yetu inayoweza kuoza lazima ivikwe uzima usioweza kuoza. Miili yetu inayoweza kufa lazima ivikwe uzima usio na mwisho.

vi.L: Vì [thân thể] hay hư nát này phải mặc lấy sự không hề hư nát, và [thân thể] hay chết này phải mặc lấy sự bất tử.
vi.B: Thân thể hay hư nát này phải mặc lấy sự không hề hư nát như một chiếc áo, và thân thể hay chết này phải mặc lấy sự bất tử.
vi.R: Thân thể có thể mục nát của chúng ta phải được mặc lấy một sự sống không thể mục nát. Thân thể có thể chết của chúng ta phải được mặc lấy một sự sống không bao giờ chấm dứt.

ko.L: 이 썩을 [몸]이 썩지 않을 것을 입고, 이 죽을 [몸]이 죽지 않을 것을 입어야 하기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 이 썩을 몸은 썩지 않을 것을 옷처럼 입어야 하고, 이 죽을 몸은 죽지 않을 것을 입어야 합니다.
ko.R: 썩는 우리 몸은 결코 썩지 않는 생명으로 옷 입어야 합니다. 죽는 우리 몸은 영원히 끝나지 않는 생명으로 옷 입어야 합니다.

pt.L: Pois é necessário [que] este [corpo] corruptível se revista de incorruptibilidade, e [que] este [corpo] mortal se revista de imortalidade.
pt.B: Este corpo corruptível precisa se revestir de incorruptibilidade como de uma roupa, e este corpo mortal precisa se revestir de imortalidade.
pt.R: Os nossos corpos que se decompõem precisam ser vestidos com uma vida que não se decompõe. Os nossos corpos que morrem precisam ser vestidos com uma vida que nunca acaba.

decisions.choice: it is necessary: it must happen in God's plan
decisions.reason: δεῖ speaks of what God has determined, as in verse 25 ("he must reign"). The change of verse 52 must happen because flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom (verse 50).

decisions.choice: put on: be clothed with, as with a garment
decisions.reason: ἐνδύσασθαι is the verb for putting on clothes. Paul pictures the body being clothed with imperishability, not thrown away. In 2 Corinthians 5:2-4 he uses the same picture of the new body put on over the old.

decisions.choice: this perishable, this mortal: this present body, the same body that is raised
decisions.reason: τοῦτο ("this") points to the present body, perhaps as if Paul pointed to himself. The body that is changed is the one that now lives and dies.

decisions.choice: mortal: able to die; immortality: being beyond death
decisions.reason: ἀθανασίαν means deathlessness. Only God has it by nature (1 Timothy 6:16); here he gives it to the bodies of his people.

decisions.choice: [body] (L); body, like a garment (B); our bodies, clothed with a life (R)
alternatives: this perishable must put on imperishability
decisions.reason: The Greek has neuter adjectives; the body is meant (m3). Balanced adds "like a garment" once, so that the picture of clothing is not missed (m2). Readable says what immortality is.

decisions.choice: esto corruptible, esto mortal, no brackets
decisions.reason: The Greek has neuter adjectives, "this perishable", "this mortal". Spanish can say the same with the neuter "esto", so Literal needs no supplied word where the English adds "[body]"; Balanced says "este cuerpo".

decisions.choice: kutokufa
decisions.reason: "Kutokufa" (immortality, being beyond death) is the word Swahili Romans 2:7 uses; it pairs with "kutoharibika" as the Greek pairs the two words.

decisions.choice: "mặc lấy" for endyo; "sự bất tử" for athanasia; "hay chết" for thnetos
decisions.reason: "Mặc lấy" is the verb of the Vietnamese Ephesians 4:24 and Colossians 3:10 for putting on, keeping the picture of clothing (m2). "Bất tử" is the plain word for immortal; "hư nát" stays for phthora, so the two pairs of the verse remain distinct.

decisions.choice: "입다" for "put on" at every level, here and in verse 54
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as putting on clothes: the body is clothed, not thrown away; the same Korean verb as "wear" in verse 49. "덧입다" is kept for the doubled verb of 2 Corinthians 5:2-4.

source.text: ὅταν δὲ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀθανασίαν, τότε γενήσεται ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος· Κατεπόθη ὁ θάνατος εἰς νῖκος.

records.literal_gloss: When but the perishable this puts on imperishability and the mortal this puts on immortality, then will come about the word that has been written: Was swallowed up the death into victory.

en.L: But when this perishable [body] puts on imperishability and this mortal [body] puts on immortality, then the word that is written will come about: "Death was swallowed up in victory."
en.B: When this perishable body has put on imperishability and this mortal body has put on immortality, then the words written in Scripture will come true: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."
en.R: When our bodies that decay are clothed with a life that cannot decay, and our bodies that die are clothed with a life that never ends, then what Scripture says will come true: "Victory has swallowed up death."

fr.L: Mais quand ce [corps] corruptible aura revêtu l’incorruptibilité et que ce [corps] mortel aura revêtu l’immortalité, alors s’accomplira la parole qui est écrite : « La mort a été engloutie dans la victoire. »
fr.B: Quand ce corps périssable aura été revêtu de ce qui ne périt pas, et ce corps mortel de l’immortalité, alors se réaliseront ces paroles de l’Écriture : « La mort a été engloutie dans la victoire. »
fr.R: Quand notre corps qui se décompose sera habillé d’une vie qui ne se décompose pas, et notre corps qui meurt d’une vie qui ne finit jamais, alors ce que dit l’Écriture se réalisera : « La victoire a englouti la mort. »

es.L: Y cuando esto corruptible se vista de incorrupción y esto mortal se vista de inmortalidad, entonces se cumplirá la palabra que está escrita: «La muerte fue devorada en victoria».
es.B: Cuando este cuerpo corruptible se haya revestido de incorrupción y este cuerpo mortal se haya revestido de inmortalidad, entonces se cumplirá lo que está escrito: «La muerte ha sido devorada por la victoria».
es.R: Cuando nuestros cuerpos que se descomponen sean revestidos de una vida que no se descompone, y nuestros cuerpos que mueren sean revestidos de una vida que nunca termina, entonces se cumplirá lo que dice la Escritura: «La victoria se ha tragado a la muerte».

sw.L: Lakini [mwili] huu unaoharibika utakapovaa kutoharibika, na [mwili] huu unaokufa utakapovaa kutokufa, ndipo litakapotimia neno lililoandikwa: "Kifo kimemezwa katika ushindi."
sw.B: Mwili huu unaoharibika utakapokuwa umevaa kutoharibika, na mwili huu unaokufa utakapokuwa umevaa kutokufa, ndipo maneno yaliyoandikwa katika Maandiko yatatimia: "Kifo kimemezwa katika ushindi."
sw.R: Miili yetu inayooza itakapovikwa uzima usioweza kuoza, na miili yetu inayokufa itakapovikwa uzima usio na mwisho, ndipo yale yanayosemwa na Maandiko yatatimia: "Ushindi umekimeza kifo."

vi.L: Nhưng khi [thân thể] hay hư nát này mặc lấy sự không hề hư nát và [thân thể] hay chết này mặc lấy sự bất tử, thì lời đã chép sẽ được ứng nghiệm: "Sự chết đã bị nuốt mất trong chiến thắng."
vi.B: Khi thân thể hay hư nát này đã mặc lấy sự không hề hư nát và thân thể hay chết này đã mặc lấy sự bất tử, thì lời đã được chép trong Kinh Thánh sẽ được ứng nghiệm: "Sự chết đã bị nuốt mất trong chiến thắng."
vi.R: Khi thân thể có thể mục nát của chúng ta được mặc lấy sự sống không thể mục nát, và thân thể có thể chết của chúng ta được mặc lấy sự sống không bao giờ chấm dứt, thì điều Kinh Thánh nói sẽ thành sự thật: "Chiến thắng đã nuốt mất sự chết."

ko.L: 이 썩을 [몸]이 썩지 않을 것을 입고 이 죽을 [몸]이 죽지 않을 것을 입을 때에, 그때에 "죽음이 삼켜져 승리에 이르렀다" 하고 기록된 말씀이 이루어질 것입니다.
ko.B: 이 썩을 몸이 썩지 않을 것을 입고, 이 죽을 몸이 죽지 않을 것을 입게 될 때, 그때에 성경에 기록된 말씀이 이루어질 것입니다. "죽음이 삼켜져 승리로 끝났다."
ko.R: 썩는 우리 몸이 결코 썩지 않는 생명으로 옷 입고, 죽는 우리 몸이 영원히 끝나지 않는 생명으로 옷 입을 때, 성경에 기록된 말씀이 이루어질 것입니다. "승리가 죽음을 삼켜 버렸다."

pt.L: Mas, quando este [corpo] corruptível se revestir de incorruptibilidade e este [corpo] mortal se revestir de imortalidade, então se cumprirá a palavra que está escrita: "A morte foi engolida na vitória."
pt.B: Quando este corpo corruptível tiver se revestido de incorruptibilidade e este corpo mortal tiver se revestido de imortalidade, então vão se cumprir as palavras que estão nas Escrituras: "A morte foi engolida na vitória."
pt.R: Quando os nossos corpos que se decompõem forem vestidos com uma vida que não se decompõe, e os nossos corpos que morrem forem vestidos com uma vida que nunca acaba, então vai acontecer o que as Escrituras dizem: "A vitória engoliu a morte."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 25:8, in a Greek form that differs from the Hebrew
alternatives: a saying with no Scripture behind it
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Isaiah 25:8 God is the subject: he will swallow up death forever, on the day he prepares a feast for all peoples. Paul's Greek is passive and says "into victory" where the Hebrew has "forever"; the Hebrew word for "forever" was also used for victory in later Hebrew and Aramaic. Paul's wording does not follow the Septuagint, which reads differently, but agrees with later Greek versions of Isaiah.

decisions.choice: was swallowed up: death completely done away with, by God
decisions.reason: The past tense Κατεπόθη describes the victory as finished. The passive leaves God unnamed, as the Hebrew names him. Death, which swallowed up the living, is itself swallowed up.

decisions.choice: then: the prophecy will be fully fulfilled at the resurrection
decisions.reason: τότε ("then") ties the fulfillment to the moment the dead are raised and the living changed. Death is not yet abolished (verse 26).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: both clauses, perishable and mortal
alternatives: only the clause about the mortal
the two clauses in the other order
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack the first clause, about the perishable putting on imperishability, and a few put the clauses in the other order. Because the two clauses end alike, a copyist's eye could easily skip from one to the other. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Victory has swallowed up death (R)
alternatives: Death has been swallowed up in victory
decisions.reason: Readable makes the sentence active, which is easier to follow; it keeps the picture of swallowing.

decisions.choice: the words written in Scripture (B); what Scripture says (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Scriptures, which the phrase "what is written" means.

decisions.choice: devorada (L, B); se ha tragado (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures death swallowed up and done away with (m2). "Devorar" keeps the picture in Literal and Balanced; Readable turns the sentence round, "la victoria se ha tragado a la muerte", as the English does.

decisions.choice: the words of Isaiah 25:8 in the plain style, with death as the subject (L, B) and victory as the subject (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the passive as death done away with by God; the English Readable makes victory the subject, as Korean Readable does.

decisions.choice: engolir
decisions.reason: "Tragar" is the traditional word in this verse, but it is literary today; "engolir" is the everyday verb for swallowing and keeps the picture of death, which swallowed the living, being swallowed itself (m2).

source.text: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ νῖκος;

records.literal_gloss: Where of you, O death, the victory?

en.L: Where, O death, [is] your victory?
en.B: Death, where is your victory?
en.R: Death, where is your victory now?

fr.L: Où, ô mort, [est] ta victoire ?
fr.B: Mort, où est ta victoire ?
fr.R: Mort, où est-elle maintenant, ta victoire ?

es.L: ¿Dónde [está], oh muerte, tu victoria?
es.B: Muerte, ¿dónde está tu victoria?
es.R: Muerte, ¿dónde está ahora tu victoria?

sw.L: Uko wapi, ewe kifo, ushindi wako?
sw.B: Kifo, ushindi wako uko wapi?
sw.R: Kifo, ushindi wako uko wapi sasa?

vi.L: Hỡi sự chết, chiến thắng của ngươi ở đâu?
vi.B: Hỡi sự chết, đâu là chiến thắng của ngươi?
vi.R: Này sự chết, bây giờ chiến thắng của ngươi đâu rồi?

ko.L: "죽음아, 너의 승리가 어디 있느냐?"
ko.B: "죽음아, 네 승리가 어디 있느냐?"
ko.R: "죽음아, 이제 네 승리가 어디 있느냐?"

pt.L: Onde, ó morte, [está] a sua vitória?
pt.B: Morte, onde está a sua vitória?
pt.R: Morte, onde está agora a sua vitória?

decisions.choice: Hosea 13:14, adapted
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Hosea 13:14 the questions are "Where are your plagues, O death? Where is your destruction, O grave?" In Hosea they may call death's plagues down on Israel or mock death; the meaning there is debated. The Septuagint has "penalty" in the first question. Paul uses "victory", taking up the word of Isaiah 25:8 in verse 54, and makes these questions a taunt over defeated death.

decisions.choice: a taunt: death has no victory left
decisions.reason: The question needs no answer. Death is spoken to as an enemy (verse 26) that has lost.

decisions.choice: O death (L); Death (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the old form of address; Balanced and Readable simply name death. Readable adds "now" to show that the question mocks a defeated enemy (m2).

decisions.choice: "Hỡi sự chết" (L, B), "Này sự chết" (R), with "ngươi" for death addressed
decisions.reason: Death is taunted as an enemy (m2); "ngươi" is the old form of address used in the Vietnamese Romans for those God or a speaker addresses from above, and carries the taunt without the rudeness of "mầy".

decisions.choice: death addressed with "죽음아" and the plain style ("어디 있느냐?")
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the words as a taunt to death as a defeated enemy; Korean addresses it with the plain vocative "-아" and 해라체. "사망" is the older church word; "죽음" is the word of the chapter.

decisions.choice: a sua vitória (você forms for death)
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to death as to a defeated enemy (m2). In this translation "tu" is kept for God and Christ and for God speaking (style section 4); a person taunting a personified enemy uses the ordinary "você" forms, so "sua" in both questions. "Onde está, ó morte, a tua vitória?" is the wording readers know from older Bibles; it is not used, so that "tu" keeps its single use. "Ó" stays at Literal, as the English keeps "O death".

source.text: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον;

records.literal_gloss: Where of you, O death, the sting?

en.L: Where, O death, [is] your sting?
en.B: Death, where is your sting?
en.R: Death, where is your sting now?

fr.L: Où, ô mort, [est] ton aiguillon ?
fr.B: Mort, où est ton aiguillon ?
fr.R: Mort, où est-il maintenant, ton dard ?

es.L: ¿Dónde [está], oh muerte, tu aguijón?
es.B: Muerte, ¿dónde está tu aguijón?
es.R: Muerte, ¿dónde está ahora tu aguijón?

sw.L: Uko wapi, ewe kifo, mwiba wako?
sw.B: Kifo, mwiba wako uko wapi?
sw.R: Kifo, mwiba wako uko wapi sasa?

vi.L: Hỡi sự chết, nọc độc của ngươi ở đâu?
vi.B: Hỡi sự chết, đâu là nọc độc của ngươi?
vi.R: Này sự chết, bây giờ nọc độc của ngươi đâu rồi?

ko.L: "죽음아, 너의 독침이 어디 있느냐?"
ko.B: "죽음아, 네 독침이 어디 있느냐?"
ko.R: "죽음아, 이제 네 독침이 어디 있느냐?"

pt.L: Onde, ó morte, [está] o seu ferrão?
pt.B: Morte, onde está o seu ferrão?
pt.R: Morte, onde está agora o seu ferrão?

decisions.choice: sting: the sting of a scorpion or insect, which wounds and kills
decisions.reason: κέντρον can be the sting of a scorpion (Revelation 9:10) or a farmer's goad (Acts 26:14). Here it is death's weapon, and verse 56 says what it is.

decisions.choice: death named again where Hosea has the grave
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Hosea 13:14 speaks to "Sheol", the grave or the place of the dead, in the second question. Paul speaks to death both times.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "death" both times, victory first and sting second
alternatives: the two questions in the other order, with "grave" in place of "death" in the second
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts put the question about the sting first and speak to the grave (Hades) in the second, as the King James Version does. This brings the text closer to the Greek Old Testament. The earliest manuscripts support the SBLGNT. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: O death (L); Death (B, R); now (R)
decisions.reason: As in the first question.

decisions.choice: aiguillon (L, B); dard (R); the same in verse 56
decisions.reason: "Aiguillon" is the French word for the sting of an insect or scorpion and the traditional one here; Readable says "dard", the everyday word for the part that stings (m1). "Piqûre" would name the wound rather than the weapon.

decisions.choice: aguijón
decisions.reason: The word is the sting of a scorpion or insect (m1); Spanish "aguijón" is that sting, and verse 56 keeps it.

decisions.choice: mwiba
decisions.reason: "Mwiba" is the sting of a scorpion or bee as well as a thorn, the thing that wounds and kills (meaning decision); "uchungu" (pain) would lose the picture, which verse 56 takes up.

decisions.choice: "독침" for the sting, here and in verse 56
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes the sting of a scorpion that wounds and kills; "독침" (poison sting) says it in one current word.

decisions.choice: o ferrão
decisions.reason: The sense is the sting of a scorpion or insect (m1), which is "ferrão" in Portuguese. "Aguilhão", the traditional word here, is first of all a farmer's goad, the other sense m1 sets aside. Verse 56 follows.

source.text: τὸ δὲ κέντρον τοῦ θανάτου ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἡ δὲ δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος·

records.literal_gloss: The and sting of the death [is] the sin, the and power of the sin [is] the law;

en.L: Now the sting of death [is] sin, and the power of sin [is] the law.
en.B: Death's sting is sin, and what gives sin its power is the law.
en.R: Death stings and kills people because of sin. And sin has power because of the law.

fr.L: Or l’aiguillon de la mort, [c’est] le péché, et la puissance du péché, [c’est] la Loi.
fr.B: L’aiguillon de la mort, c’est le péché, et ce qui donne au péché sa puissance, c’est la Loi.
fr.R: La mort pique et tue les gens à cause du péché. Et le péché a de la puissance à cause de la Loi.

es.L: Ahora bien, el aguijón de la muerte [es] el pecado, y el poder del pecado [es] la ley.
es.B: El aguijón de la muerte es el pecado, y lo que da poder al pecado es la ley.
es.R: La muerte pica y mata a la gente por causa del pecado. Y el pecado tiene poder por causa de la ley.

sw.L: Basi mwiba wa kifo [ni] dhambi, na nguvu ya dhambi [ni] sheria.
sw.B: Mwiba wa kifo ni dhambi, na kinachoipa dhambi nguvu yake ni sheria.
sw.R: Kifo huwachoma watu na kuwaua kwa sababu ya dhambi. Na dhambi ina nguvu kwa sababu ya sheria.

vi.L: Nọc độc của sự chết là tội lỗi, và quyền lực của tội lỗi là luật pháp.
vi.B: Nọc độc của sự chết là tội lỗi, và điều cho tội lỗi quyền lực là luật pháp.
vi.R: Sự chết chích và giết chết con người là vì tội lỗi. Và tội lỗi có quyền lực là vì luật pháp.

ko.L: 죽음의 독침은 죄이고, 죄의 힘은 율법입니다.
ko.B: 죽음의 독침은 죄이고, 죄에 힘을 주는 것은 율법입니다.
ko.R: 죽음은 죄 때문에 사람을 찌르고 죽입니다. 그리고 죄는 율법 때문에 힘을 얻습니다.

pt.L: Ora, o ferrão da morte [é] o pecado, e o poder do pecado [é] a Lei.
pt.B: O ferrão da morte é o pecado, e o que dá poder ao pecado é a Lei.
pt.R: A morte fere e mata as pessoas por causa do pecado. E o pecado tem poder por causa da Lei.

decisions.choice: sin is the sting by which death wounds and kills
decisions.reason: Death has its deadly power because of sin: sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin (Romans 5:12); the wages of sin is death (Romans 6:23).

decisions.choice: the law gives sin its power: it shows sin for what it is, stirs it up and condemns it
decisions.reason: Paul says briefly here what he explains in Romans 7:7-13: the law is holy (Romans 7:12), but sin uses the commandment to bring death, and the law counts sin against the sinner (Romans 5:13, 20). νόμος is the law given through Moses.

decisions.choice: what gives sin its power (B); sin has power because of the law (R)
alternatives: the power of sin is the law
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the law relates to sin; Readable also says what the sting does.

decisions.choice: la Loi, capitalised
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the capital marks the Law of Moses, which is what gives sin its power here (m2), not law in general.

source.text: τῷ δὲ θεῷ χάρις τῷ διδόντι ἡμῖν τὸ νῖκος διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: To the but God thanks, the [one] giving to us the victory through the Lord of us Jesus Christ.

en.B: But thanks be to God, for through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives us the victory.
en.R: We thank God, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives us the victory over death through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Mais grâce [soit rendue] à Dieu, qui nous donne la victoire par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Mais grâce soit rendue à Dieu, car c’est par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous donne la victoire.
fr.R: Nous remercions Dieu, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous donne la victoire sur la mort par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

es.L: Pero gracias [sean] a Dios, que nos da la victoria por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Pero gracias a Dios, que por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}} nos da la victoria.
es.R: Damos gracias a Dios, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos da la victoria sobre la muerte por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Lakini shukrani [ziwe] kwa Mungu, anayetupa ushindi kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Lakini Mungu ashukuriwe, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hutupa ushindi kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Tunamshukuru Mungu, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hutupa ushindi juu ya kifo kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

vi.L: Nhưng tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng ban cho chúng ta sự chiến thắng qua Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Nhưng tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời, vì qua Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban cho chúng ta sự chiến thắng.
vi.R: Chúng ta cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban cho chúng ta sự chiến thắng sự chết qua Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.

ko.L: 그러나 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통하여 우리에게 승리를 주시는 하나님께 감사를 [드립니다].
ko.B: 그러나 하나님께 감사드립니다. 하나님께서는 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통해 우리에게 승리를 주십니다.
ko.R: 우리는 하나님께 감사드립니다. 하나님께서는 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통해 우리에게 죽음을 이기는 승리를 주십니다.

pt.L: Mas graças [sejam dadas] a Deus, que nos dá a vitória por meio do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.
pt.B: Mas graças a Deus, pois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} nos dá a vitória por meio do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.
pt.R: Nós agradecemos a Deus, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} nos dá a vitória sobre a morte por meio do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.

decisions.choice: thanks: gratitude given to God
decisions.reason: χάρις usually means grace, but with "to God" and no verb it is the set phrase for giving thanks, as in 2 Corinthians 2:14; 8:16; 9:15 and Romans 6:17. So the key term is not rendered "grace" here.

decisions.choice: who gives: God gives the victory now, and it will be seen in full at the resurrection
decisions.reason: The present participle διδόντι describes God as the one who gives the victory. It is already given through Christ's resurrection, and its fullness comes when death is swallowed up (verse 54).

decisions.choice: the victory: the victory over death and sin of verses 54-56
decisions.reason: The article points back to "victory" in verses 54 and 55.

decisions.choice: thanks; thank (R)
decisions.reason: The key term is rendered "thanks" here because the sense is gratitude (m1).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: victory over death (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says which victory is meant (m3).

decisions.choice: grâce soit rendue (L, B); nous remercions (R)
decisions.reason: The sense is gratitude (m1). "Grâce soit rendue à Dieu" is the French expression of thanks that keeps the key term "grâce" visible at Literal and Balanced; Readable uses the plain verb.

decisions.choice: shukrani
decisions.reason: The Greek word is thanks to God here (meaning decision), so "shukrani" as in 10:30, not the key term "neema" (grace).

decisions.choice: "tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời" (L, B), "cảm tạ" (R) for charis to theo
decisions.reason: Here charis is thanks, not grace (m1); Vietnamese has the ordinary phrase for thanks to God, and "ân điển" is kept for grace.

decisions.choice: "감사" at every level for the thanks
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word usually translated "grace" as the set phrase for giving thanks, as in 10:30; Korean says "감사".

decisions.choice: graças a Deus
decisions.reason: Portuguese gives thanks with "graças", the plural of "graça", so Literal and Balanced say "thanks" (m1) and still keep the key term's word in sight. Readable says "agradecemos", as the English Readable says "We thank".

source.text: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί, ἑδραῖοι γίνεσθε, ἀμετακίνητοι, περισσεύοντες ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ τοῦ κυρίου πάντοτε, εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κόπος ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔστιν κενὸς ἐν κυρίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: So then, brothers of me beloved, firm be, immovable, abounding in the work of the Lord always, knowing that the toil of you not is empty in [the] Lord.

en.L: So then, my beloved {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, be firm, immovable, abounding in the work of the Lord always, knowing that your toil is not empty in [the] Lord.
en.B: So then, my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, be firm and unshakable, always doing more and more in the work of the Lord, since you know that in the Lord your hard work is never wasted.
en.R: So, my dear {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, stand strong, and do not let anything shake you. Always give your best to the work the Lord has given you. You know that nothing you do as people joined to the Lord is wasted.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} bien-aimés, soyez fermes, inébranlables, abondant toujours dans l’œuvre du Seigneur, sachant que votre peine n’est pas vaine dans le Seigneur.
fr.B: Ainsi donc, mes chers {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, soyez fermes et inébranlables, et progressez toujours dans l’œuvre du Seigneur, car vous savez que, dans le Seigneur, votre labeur n’est jamais inutile.
fr.R: Alors, mes chers {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, tenez bon, et ne laissez rien vous ébranler. Donnez toujours le meilleur de vous-mêmes dans le travail que le Seigneur vous a confié. Vous le savez : rien de ce que vous faites comme personnes unies au Seigneur n’est perdu.

es.L: Así que, hermanos míos amados, {{plural_you:estén|estad}} firmes, inconmovibles, abundando siempre en la obra del Señor, sabiendo que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} trabajo no es vacío en [el] Señor.
es.B: Por lo tanto, mis queridos hermanos, {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} firmes e inconmovibles, progresando siempre en la obra del Señor, pues {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que en el Señor {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} esfuerzo nunca es en vano.
es.R: Así que, mis queridos hermanos, {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} firmes, y no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nada {{plural_you:los|os}} haga tambalear. {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} siempre lo mejor de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en la obra que el Señor {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado. {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} que nada de lo que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} como personas unidas al Señor es en vano.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, ndugu zangu wapendwa, kuweni imara, msiotikisika, mkizidi katika kazi ya Bwana siku zote, mkijua kwamba taabu yenu si bure katika Bwana.
sw.B: Basi, ndugu zangu wapendwa, simameni imara bila kutikisika, mkizidi kufanya kazi ya Bwana siku zote, kwa kuwa mnajua kwamba katika Bwana kazi yenu ngumu haipotei bure.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, ndugu zangu wapendwa, simameni imara, na msikubali kitu chochote kiwatikise. Siku zote fanyeni kwa bidii kazi ambayo Bwana amewapa. Mnajua kwamba hakuna jambo mnalofanya kama watu walioungana na Bwana linalopotea bure.

vi.L: Vậy, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} yêu dấu của tôi, hãy vững vàng, không lay chuyển, luôn luôn dư dật trong công việc của Chúa, vì biết rằng công khó của anh chị em trong Chúa không phải là vô ích.
vi.B: Vậy, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} thân yêu của tôi, hãy đứng vững, không gì lay chuyển được, luôn luôn làm việc Chúa ngày càng nhiều hơn, vì anh chị em biết rằng trong Chúa, công khó của anh chị em không bao giờ uổng phí.
vi.R: Vậy, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} thân yêu của tôi, hãy đứng vững, và đừng để điều gì làm anh chị em lay chuyển. Hãy luôn dốc hết sức cho công việc Chúa đã giao cho anh chị em. Anh chị em biết rằng không điều gì anh chị em làm như những người gắn bó với Chúa lại là uổng phí.

ko.L: 그러므로 나의 사랑하는 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 굳건하고 흔들리지 않는 사람이 되어, 언제나 주님의 일에 넘치도록 힘쓰십시오. 여러분의 수고가 주님 안에서 헛되지 않다는 것을 여러분이 알기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 나의 사랑하는 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 굳게 서서 흔들리지 마십시오. 언제나 주님의 일에 더욱더 힘쓰십시오. 여러분이 알다시피, 주님 안에서 여러분의 수고는 결코 헛되지 않습니다.
ko.R: 그러니 나의 사랑하는 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 굳세게 서십시오. 아무것도 여러분을 흔들지 못하게 하십시오. 주님께서 여러분에게 맡기신 일에 언제나 최선을 다하십시오. 여러분이 주님께 속한 사람으로서 하는 일은 무엇이든 헛되지 않다는 것을 여러분은 압니다.

pt.L: Assim, meus amados {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, sejam firmes, inabaláveis, abundando sempre na obra do Senhor, sabendo que o trabalho de vocês não é vazio no Senhor.
pt.B: Por isso, meus queridos {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, sejam firmes e inabaláveis, fazendo cada vez mais na obra do Senhor, pois vocês sabem que, no Senhor, o esforço de vocês nunca é desperdiçado.
pt.R: Por isso, meus queridos {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, fiquem firmes e não deixem que nada abale vocês. Deem sempre o melhor de vocês no trabalho que o Senhor lhes deu. Vocês sabem que nada do que fazem como pessoas unidas ao Senhor é desperdiçado.

decisions.choice: so then: the conclusion of the whole chapter
decisions.reason: Ὥστε draws out what follows from the sure hope of resurrection: since Christ has been raised and death will be swallowed up, what believers do now is not lost.

decisions.choice: firm, immovable: holding fast to the gospel and its hope
decisions.reason: ἑδραῖοι is something firmly seated; ἀμετακίνητοι is what cannot be moved from its place. The chapter began with the gospel the Corinthians stand in and must hold fast (verses 1-2), and some were denying the resurrection (verse 12). Colossians 1:23 uses similar words for not being moved from the hope of the gospel.

decisions.choice: the work of the Lord: the work the Lord gives and that is done for him
alternatives: only the work the Lord himself does
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of building up the church as work done for the Lord (3:9-15; 16:10). The genitive may include both the Lord's ownership of the work and its being done for him.

decisions.choice: toil: hard work to the point of weariness; not empty: not without result
decisions.reason: κόπος is labor that tires. κενὸς ("empty") takes up verses 10 and 14: God's grace to Paul was not empty, and if Christ had not been raised, preaching and faith would be empty.

decisions.choice: in the Lord: as people joined to the Lord
decisions.reason: ἐν κυρίῳ ("in the Lord") says that their work is done in union with the risen Lord, and so it will last.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The plural addresses the whole church, men and women.

decisions.choice: beloved (L); dear (B, R); doing more and more (B); give your best (R)
decisions.reason: περισσεύοντες means to overflow or have more than enough; with "always", it means to keep growing in the work, as in 1 Thessalonians 4:1, 10.

decisions.choice: the work the Lord has given you; as people joined to the Lord (R)
alternatives: the work of the Lord; in the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two phrases (m3, m5). "The work the Lord has given you" chooses one side of an uncertain genitive.

decisions.choice: amados
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "amados" for the Greek word for beloved; Balanced and Readable say "queridos", the ordinary Spanish for dear friends.

decisions.choice: ndugu zangu wapendwa, no gender span
decisions.reason: As 15:1: "ndugu" already includes sisters, and "wapendwa" (beloved) does not mark sex.

decisions.choice: "헛되지 않다" at every level, the word of verses 10 and 14
decisions.reason: The meaning decision ties "not empty" to verses 10 and 14, where Korean says "헛되다".
